subject: Network lattice: boundary & SIG evidence request
messages:
From: Adam Parker <adam.parker@veridian.com>
To: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.com>
Cc: security@acmehealth.org
Date: 2026-10-01T14:22:00-07:00
Subject: Request: network architecture overview and SIG/CAIQ evidence

Hi Ava,

Hope you’re well. Veridian is running a SIG/CAIQ/SOC 2 review for our upcoming procurement and we need a concise architecture package that explains how Redwood’s Dedicated/Private deployments enforce network and tenancy isolation. Specifically we’re asking for: 

- A high-level network diagram for both Dedicated and Private deployments (control plane vs data plane).
- A short narrative on control-plane segmentation and how it’s separated from customer data paths.
- Evidence or mapping to SIG controls (network isolation, egress controls, perimeter).
- Any redacted examples or artifacts you can share (IP ranges, ACL patterns, diagram exports).

Can you confirm whether you can provide this as a single packaged deliverable (diagram + mapping table + short narrative) by Oct 12? Our audit team will need enough detail to map to SIG v2025.

Thanks — appreciate it.

Adam Parker
Head of Security, Veridian Health
adam.parker@veridian.com

Thanks for the clear ask. We can put together a focused package that includes: a redacted network diagram for Dedicated and Private, a 2-page narrative describing control-plane vs data-plane separation, and a mapping table to the SIG/CAIQ controls you called out.

Proposed plan:
- Kimberly will produce the diagram exports (PDF + PNG) and a mapping spreadsheet by Oct 6.
- I’ll write the 2-page narrative and coordinate an internal review by Oct 8.
- Marissa will package everything and deliver a single ZIP and Drive link to you by Oct 9 with an option to add redacted iptables/ACL examples if needed.

Kimberly / Marissa / Jonas — please review the timeline and confirm you can hit these milestones. If we need more time for redaction of flow logs or ACL examples, flag it here.

Adam — is the Oct 9 bundle acceptable as a first deliverable (we can follow up with additional artifacts by Oct 12 if needed)? Also let us know if your auditors require any specific format (PDF, XLSX, CAIQ mapping CSV).

Best,

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-04T16:45:00-07:00
Subject: Draft: network lattice diagram + SIG mapping (for review)

Team — attaching drafts for review. I made the following choices to keep the packet audit-friendly while minimizing exposure of sensitive routing data:

Attachments: network-lattice-draft.pdf (diagram export), sig-mapping-table.xlsx (mapping to SIG/CAIQ), lattice-annotation-v2.png (annotated zoom)

Notes on diagram:
- The diagram shows control-plane endpoints in a separate VPC (Control-VPC) with mutual TLS between control-plane services and dedicated tenant-facing workers.
- Data plane (inference traffic) is shown in customer-dedicated subnets when on Dedicated; for Private we show the customer VPC + private control-plane peering (redacted peering IDs).
- Egress paths are annotated; default-deny with egress-proxy for telemetry is our pattern.

SIG mapping highlights (sheet tab: Summary):
- NET-01: segmentation rationale and links to diagram figures.
- NET-03: egress controls — description + reference to proxy IP ranges (redacted).
- NET-06: control plane authentication and cert rotation cadence.

Questions for review:
- Do we want to include a sanitized iptables example in the first bundle or reserve that for a follow-up?
- Jonas: can you confirm the language about fallback model variants (we mention automatic fallback to a lower tier model when Dedicated capacity is constrained) — auditors sometimes treat fallback designs as control exceptions.

If I don’t hear objections I’ll finalize visuals and push to Drive for packaging on Oct 6.

—Kimberly
Kimberly Park
Principal Security Architect, Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Subject: Fwd: Draft: network lattice diagram + SIG mapping (packaged deliverable)

Adam — forwarding the finalized package for your intake team. Quick summary below; full artifacts and mapping are attached and available on Drive (link included).

What we’re delivering (first bundle):
- network-lattice-draft.pdf — high-level diagram for Dedicated and Private (redacted IDs).
- lattice-annotation-v2.png — zoomed-in annotation for control/data-plane separation.
- sig-mapping-table.xlsx — control-by-control mapping (sheet tabs: Summary, NET, AUTH, EGRESS).

Key points called out in the narrative (2-page PDF inside the package):
- Control plane is logically and network-wise separated in a Control-VPC with mutual TLS and strict ACLs; only authenticated control-plane services may initiate config changes.
- Data plane for Dedicated uses tenant-dedicated subnets; for Private we document the customer-managed VPC peering model and optional air-gapped deployment.
- Egress is default-deny; telemetry egress flows through a proxy with allowlist (we’ve redacted IP ranges in this first package).

Delivery link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3Lattice
Attachments included: network-lattice-draft.pdf, sig-mapping-table.xlsx, lattice-annotation-v2.png

If your auditors want sanitized examples of iptables or ACL exports we can include them in a follow-up (I’ve flagged this as an optional Oct 12 deliverable).

Regards,

Marissa / team — thanks for the fast turnaround and the clear package. The diagram and the SIG mapping look good overall. A couple of quick clarifications before I close the ticket with our audit team: 

1) On the egress note you mention an "egress proxy with allowlist (redacted)" — can you provide either a redacted ACL example or a one-page summary of how egress is enforced (proxy rules, host-level vs network-level enforcement)? A short sanitized example will save follow-up questions.
2) For Private deployments where you mention "customer-managed VPC peering," can you confirm whether control-plane telemetry is ever routed over the customer VPC or if it always traverses a control-plane peering that Redwood controls (we need to ensure telemetry does not traverse customer-managed internet gateways).

If you can drop those two small items (sanitized ACL example + one-sentence telemetry path confirmation) into the Drive folder I’ll mark the package as accepted by Oct 12.

Adam Parker
Head of Security, Veridian Health
